To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the globular domain of H1 and H1 itself bind strongly to four-way junctions, with affinities that are comparable to those of other DNA binding proteins, such as the high mobility group proteins, and are much higher than those of other histones.

1) the globular domains of H1 and H1 bind to a four-way DNA junction with a higher affinity than the intact histone; 2) the binding of intact H1 to a DNA junction is inhibited by cationic species such as Mg2+ or spermidine, whereas this is not true for the binding of H5 to the same junction; 3) the binding of H3 globular domain to a four-way junction is not inhibited by Mg2+
histones H1, H5, and their globular domain bind to the junction of four DNA strands, and that the binding is inhibited by cationic molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of the linker histone in the organization of chromatin, particularly the role of the globular domain in chromatin folding and the role of the N-terminal domain in the regulation of transcription.
the interaction of the linker histones with DNA crossoves.
the binding of the globular domain of histone H1 to four-way DNA junctions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
histone binding to four-way junctions is a function of the angle formed between arms of the junction and the affinity of the protein for the junction.
the H1 and H1 globular domains are able to bind to four-way junctions and to linear duplex DNA, and that the H1 globular domain has higher affinity for four-way junctions than for linear DNA.
H5 binds more strongly to the junction than H1, and that the binding of both histones is inhibited by cation-induced changes in the con formation of the junction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the globular domain of H1 is a major component in the recognition of the junction structure, and that the N-terminal tail is not involved in this recognition.
histones H1, H5 and their respective globular domains all have a high affinity for four-way junction DNA, but the binding properties of these proteins differ.
histones H1/H5 bind to four-way junctions with high affinity, and that the binding is not simply due to electrostatic interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the globular domains of histones H5 and H1 can bind to DNA crossovers and that these interactions may be important in vivo.
the binding of H5 to the DNA junction is stronger than H1.
the binding of H5 and H1 is not only to linear DNA, but is also to the four-way junction DNA, and the binding affinity to the four-way DNA is higher than to the linear DNA.
